bundles.when_i_would_meet_it: Monday morning, pasting the data engineer job description before the 140 applications get processed.
bundles.why: I hate retyping what is already in the job description, so suggested must-haves save me time, but I could still write them by hand.

bundles.when_i_would_meet_it: Tuesday, uploading the CV batch or importing the CSV from my ATS between two interviews.
bundles.why: Without CVs read automatically I would be typing claims by hand for 140 people, which makes the tool pointless.

bundles.when_i_would_meet_it: Wednesday in a 20-minute block, going through the flagged list to confirm the shortlist for the interviews.
bundles.why: This is the core of my problem, cutting 140 applications to a shortlist quickly, and I need to find my place again after phone calls.

bundles.when_i_would_meet_it: Thursday, sending proof requests to the shortlisted people before Friday and checking uploaded documents.
bundles.why: It is useful and saves email chasing, but I can ask for certificates by email myself if I have to.

bundles.when_i_would_meet_it: Friday afternoon, approving feedback drafts for rejected candidates instead of writing dozens of emails.
bundles.why: It is a nice time saver and good for employer image, but today I mostly send short generic rejections or nothing, so it is not essential.

bundles.when_i_would_meet_it: Only when my HR lead asks for numbers in a monthly meeting; I would not open it myself.
bundles.why: It is for the HR lead and does not change my daily work much.

proof_timing.why: Asking for documents at application would scare off candidates and give me 140 piles of paperwork to handle, while asking only the shortlisted few is reasonable and manageable.
